concept.reason: Actual full mounted skeleton and adult skull reference sufficient, no concept generation.

scope: Whole animal preserving the original genus-level target: long lightly built hindlimbs and extended narrow neck. Concrete species reference D.elderae, not old D.altus label or African Dysalotosaurus.

scientific_limits.en: Original living reconstruction, not scan. Carnegie CM3392 mount includes substantial casts and sculpted restoration;2007 account reports only35% original bones and about25% newly sculpted. Head is checked against NPS adult skull cast; soft tissue, posture and missing parts remain inferred. Three metres is an approximate museum-mount display scale, not complete fossil measurement.
scientific_limits.zh: 完整活体美术复原，非扫描。Carnegie CM3392装架含大量翻模与雕塑补配，2007馆方说明原骨约35%、约25%新塑。头部另核NPS成年头骨翻模；软组织、姿态及缺失部分属推断。3米为约定展件尺度，非完整化石实测。

scale.basis: Carnegie2007 describes roughly10-foot mount; current NPS gives broad8-14foot estimates and2.4m smaller adult example. Three metres is approximate within that range.

diagnostic_targets: Slender extended neck joins small tapered beaked head to a moderately deep torso.
Long lightly built hindlimbs and narrow distal legs, distinct from stocky adult sauropodomorphs.
Short five-fingered forelimbs held free, no Iguanodon thumb spike.
Long tapering tail balances bipedal body; no horns, large predator teeth or armour.
Retain genuine neck/leg proportions versus compact short-necked Hypsilophodon, not size-only distinction.
specimen_basis: Actual Carnegie mounted skeleton side photograph and official frontal photo inspected; NPS adult skull cast image with inch scale inspected. Current NPS species name D.elderae used, original genus scope preserved.
acceptance_checks: Whole biped with extended narrow neck and long light hindlimbs readable in side view.
Head is small beaked herbivore; never copy the Ceratosaurus behind it in reference photograph.
Retain both arms/legs and full tail; no skeleton substitution.
Four standard views only; independent review checks original morphology and restored-part uncertainty.
